summary.root_cause_text: payment_provider_url was switched to internal://payments-v2 (unreachable) at the v1.4 config reload, so the worker marked orders processed without payment. v1.4 ledger sync job (batch size tuning) corrupted ledger amounts, overstating 9 entries.
recommended: Add a payment-failure alert; failures are only logged at DEBUG and orders are still marked processed.
Fix the v1.4 ledger sync batch-size bug before redeploying.
Validate payment_provider_url before it is applied.

events.text:
version: v1.4
payment_provider_url: internal://payments-v2
queue_max: 1000
worker_count: 1
sync_interval_s: 5

There seem to be two separate causes here: the payment URL config change and the v1.4 ledger sync corruption. Since rollback alone won't undo the config change, I should sequence this as rollback first, then fix the config, then repair the ledger, then reprocess.
Rolled back version v1.4 -> v1.3. Confirmed: the service is now using the new value.
payment_provider_url: 'internal://payments-v2' -> 'internal://payments-v1'. Confirmed: the service is now using the new value.
All business invariants green (health, payments, queue, worker, ledger, errors, latency).

Fix the v1.4 ledger sync batch-size bug before redeploying.
Validate payment_provider_url before it is applied.
args.summary: Two simultaneous issues began at the v1.4 rollout. The payment provider URL pointed to an unreachable payments-v2, and the v1.4 ledger sync corrupted amounts. I rolled back the version, restored the v1 provider URL, reprocessed unpaid orders and repaired the ledger. All invariants are now green.
